memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Judah could not dislodge the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem; to this day the Jebusites live there with the people of Judah - Josh 15:63 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the towns and triumphs, the chapter ends on a sobering note. Judah "could not dislodge the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem." Right in the heart of the inheritance sat an unconquered stronghold, a corner of disobedience left standing. The Jebusites remained "to this day."

Scripture is honest about this incompleteness. Judah received a vast and glorious inheritance, and yet there was a task left unfinished, ground left unclaimed. It is a recurring theme in Joshua and a sober word for us: how often we, too, leave a corner of our lives unsurrendered. We follow God faithfully in most things, yet there is that one stronghold we cannot — or will not — dislodge. And what is left unconquered tends to remain, troubling us for years.

Yet there is hope woven even into this. Jerusalem would not stay in enemy hands forever. Generations later, David would finally take it, and it would become the city of God (2 Sam 5:6-7). What one generation could not finish, God completed in His time. And the final completion belongs to Christ, who leaves no enemy undefeated. Where we fall short and cannot dislodge our own strongholds, He is able to finish what we cannot. We bring Him our unconquered corners and trust His grace and power to do what we could not (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "unconquered corner" remains unsurrendered in your life?
- Are you honest with God about the strongholds you cannot dislodge alone?
- How does Christ's power to finish what we cannot give you hope today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I confess the corners of my life I have failed to surrender to You. Thank You that You are able to finish what I cannot. I bring You my strongholds and trust Your grace. Amen.
